segments_b.text: They said, what's your religion?
I said, love.
They said, but what's your God's name?
I said, which language you speak?
Because whether it's Allah, Yahweh, Adonair, or Christ,
the light don't change.
Only the tongue do.
They divide by doctrine, we unite in soul.
One race bleeding red, one light to hold.
From the miles to the chapel, the temple to the block.
I seen God in silence and I heard Him in Glock
You praised, I pray up
She praised through the fire, but we all talk to heaven
With a soul full of desire, don't matter the book
If the heart's still pure, I see more faith in the hood
Than in rows of dust, sure, no need for roads
No need for names, we all cry the same
When we feel that flame
So I ain't judging how you bow or kneel
Just as long as your love and your faith be real
Many names, but one flame
Different paths, but the light don't change
We all bleed, we all break, but love's a prayer no devil can fake
From Mecca to Jerusalem, shat down the wrong, we all looking for a way to get home
Ain't about the label, it's about the grace, one guy, one love, one human race
I broke bread with a rabbi, prayed peace with a shake
Hugged a priest in the dark with my soul, did it break
A Buddhist talk, calm, a Sufi talk, breath
And the gangsta show mercy on the heads of dead
Don't box my belief, I ain't paid for that shit
I wo-
